newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won ends little lower on intervention.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won ends little lower on intervention.

text.p: The won closed slightly down versus the dollar on Monday after a central bank intervention in the afternoon erased earlier gains, dealers said.
The bank denied the intervention as it routinely does.
The won finished at 825.40 after opening at 824.70. It touched the bottom of 827.00.

Dealers said the local currency firmed in early trading on bullish sentiment and speculative dollar selling. But the central Bank of Korea bought dollars at an intraday high of 822.80 to cap the won's rise, they said.
"The central bank wanted to send a message to banks that the won shouldn't rise any further," said one dealer.
Traders said the won was expected to stay a range of 824 to 827 on Tuesday. The central bank set the base mid-rate for Tuesday at 825.40 versus today's 825.00.
